The plaintiffs argued that Buhari did not submit his academic certificates with his Form CF001 to the Independent National Electoral Commission. They said this breached Sections 131 and 318 of the 1999 Constitution and Section 31(3) of the Electoral Act, 2010. One plaintiff, Chike Okafor, accused Buhari of perjury and asked the court to restrain INEC from allowing him to take part in the election. The suits were heard before Justice Adeniyi Ademola, and Olanipekun was named as counsel to Buhari and the APC. Some of the suits were struck out as duplicates. The judge, however, dismissed applications by two parties to be joined as defendants. On March 25, three days before the election, he adjourned the remaining suits to April 22 and 23, keeping Buhari on the ballot. “Your colleagues are here with me, led by Kola Awodein SAN, insisting that I must fetch you out to lead them in the matter,” Olanipekun recalled Tinubu saying in the book. He said Awodein “seconded Asiwaju’s application with his own plea that I should try by all means to be in court the following day.” According to the book, Tinubu took the phone back and said: “I’ll send an aircraft to pick you up at Akure tomorrow morning. The plane will leave Lagos early in the morning with Awodein and co, pick you up at Akure to Abuja, wait for you at the tarmac till you finish in court, and when you’re done in court, you can take it to Ikere, in case you already have an airport there!” Omatseye wrote that the SAN “took it as a marching order,” describing the episode as “one ominous hour in Nigerian history.” The book, which covers the period from 1998 to 2015, from Nigeria’s return to civilian rule through the collapse of the PDP’s 16-year grip on federal power, is Omatseye’s second major political work. The book is to be reviewed by Louis Odion, with excerpts read by Ohi Alegbe, Stella Din Jacobs and Yomi Odunuga. Tinubu, a former senator who had run on the Social Democratic Party platform in the 1992 senatorial elections, returned from exile and contested the Lagos governorship under the Alliance for Democracy, winning in 1999 and beginning the political journey that would eventually lead him to the presidency in 2023. Chairman of the occasion and former Governor of Ogun State, Chief Segun Osoba, said President Tinubu’s emergence was the result of tenacity and hard work. He said what made the APC successful in 2015 was that President Tinubu decided that Buhari should be adopted as the presidential candidate. item.title: UK police arrest two men after break-in at William and Kate’s home
item.description: Two men have been arrested on suspicion of burglary, police said on Tuesday, after a reported break-in at the countryside retreat of UK royals Prince William and his wife Catherine, who were not in residence at the time. Police dogs, drones and a helicopter were deployed to the Sandringham estate in Norfolk, eastern England, after the local force received a call just before 6:00 pm (1800 GMT) on Monday of “suspicious activity”, Norfolk police said in a statement sent to AFP. Anmer Hall where William, Kate and their three children occasionally live — especially during the school holidays — was broken into, according to UK media. The 10-bedroom red-brick Georgian manor was gifted to the couple by the late Queen Elizabeth II after their marriage. The men “were arrested on the estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass”, police said. The sprawling Sandringham estate is owned by William’s father King Charles III. Police said the property “was unoccupied” at the time and the men remained in custody. William and Kate mainly live at their home on the Windsor estate, just west of London. Kensington Palace, which handles the affairs of William, the heir to the throne, told AFP they would not comment on security matters. Charles’s disgraced brother, the former prince Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, moved to Sandringham earlier this year and lives about a mile from Anmer Hall. The king ousted Andrew from his home of two decades in Windsor and stripped him of his royal titles amid the fallout from his brother’s alleged dealings with the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. – Chat with the queen – It is not the first time a royal residence has been broken into, despite the tight security surrounding the royal family. In 2024, several intruders were caught on the Windsor estate after they broke into a farm building and tried to steal a pick-up truck and a quad bike. Around Christmas 2021, a 21-year-old man with mental health issues was arrested after being caught near the queen’s apartments armed with a loaded crossbow. He admitted in court to trying to kill Elizabeth and was handed a nine-year sentence, to be served initially in the high-security Broadmoor psychiatric hospital. The most famous incident was in July 1982, when a man named Michael Fagan sneaked into Buckingham Palace and made his way to Queen Elizabeth II’s bedroom. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other federal security agencies. Amupitan reminded political parties that INEC Guidelines require them to notify the Commissioner of Police in writing of rally venues and times, and to submit the details to the Commission at least ten days in advance. He appealed to political leaders “to refrain from seeking political support by creating fear,” urging them instead to “earn public confidence through integrity and transparency.” The Chairman said the nation was at “a decisive moment” on its democratic calendar. The Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold in 53 days, on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 176,846 polling units. The Governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections will follow on Saturday, February 6, 2027. He also asked for targeted police coverage of designated mock polling centres and collation points nationwide for the Commission’s mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026. According to him, the exercise will span all 36 states and the FCT. It will test the upgraded Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and automated validation protocols on the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) “under live field conditions.” Amupitan said the Commission was scaling up to a nationwide operation involving 103.43 million verified registered voters, 57,000 newly procured BVAS devices and over 1.41 million ad hoc election personnel, hence its need for deeper operational coordination with the Police. Among other priorities, he asked the Police to lead the full activation of the “ICCES Tentacles” framework down to every Local Government Area and Registration Area (Ward). This, he said, would ensure rapid-response teams are positioned “close to flashpoints and riverine or hard-to-reach corridors.” He also sought watertight perimeter security around Registration Area Centres, polling units, collation centres and INEC offices from deployment through the final declaration of results. On disinformation, the INEC chairman warned that false alarms, fabricated security alerts and manipulated audio-visual clips were “increasingly weaponised to suppress voter turnout.” He proposed real-time joint verification channels between INEC’s Situation Room and Force Headquarters to neutralise such narratives “within minutes.” Amupitan also called on security personnel to remain professional and impartial. “Their presence should reassure citizens, not foster intimidation or suggest alignment with any political party,” he said. He thanked the Police for their role in the off-cycle elections held since he assumed office in October 2025. These comprised the governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, the FCT Area Council elections and sixteen legislative bye-elections. According to him, the polls “served as a valuable operational proving ground,” and showed that “when security planning is early, intelligence-led, and strictly neutral, voters turn out in peace and electoral disputes are sharply reduced.” Early warning signs In his remarks, the Inspector General of Police IGP, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, said recent violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and convoys, and the use of dangerous weapons had become matters of serious concern. He described these developments as “warning signs that must be addressed decisively before they escalate into a broader threat to national security.” The IGP declared that the Police have “zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the political party, candidate, personality or interest involved.” He added that the Force’s neutrality in the political process “is non-negotiable.” Disu said those who sponsor, finance or direct political violence “will be treated with the same seriousness as those who carry them out.” He assured participants that the Police would “protect the rights of all lawful political actors to organise rallies, hold meetings and participate in the democratic process.” The IGP, however, that the Force would “not hesitate to take lawful and decisive action against anyone who engages in thuggery, intimidation, assault, the use of offensive weapons or any conduct capable of disrupting public peace.” The Police chief also placed responsibility on party leaders, saying the burden of peaceful political activity “cannot be transferred entirely to the Police.” He directed National Chairmen to issue clear directives against violence and ensure compliance across their party structures. National Secretaries, he said, must facilitate compliance with notification requirements, while youth leaders must mobilise young people for constructive participation rather than expose them to manipulation. Disu said the session was intended “to move us beyond general appeals for peace towards clearly defined responsibilities and practical commitments.” He disclosed that guidelines on the conduct expected of political parties before, during and after the 2027 General Elections were presented at the meeting, and that parties would execute a Joint Peace and Security Undertaking at the end of the session. “These must not be documents signed for public display and subsequently abandoned,” he said. The IGP also urged parties to show restraint after the announcement of results, discourage reprisals and pursue any grievances through lawful judicial processes. “No political ambition is worth the life of a Nigerian”, he stressed. item.title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State. The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State. It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections. The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.” It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’ The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement. It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern. item.title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The event attracted supporters from the 14 local government areas of the state, including party faithful, women and youth groups, traditional leaders and other political stakeholders. Addressing the gathering, Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State and senator representing Zamfara West, said voting for the APC at all levels, from the presidency to the state Houses of Assembly, would enable the state to benefit from federal government projects, appointments and other interventions. He argued that Zamfara could not afford to remain in opposition in 2027, urging residents to align with the ruling party at the federal level. “I urge you, the good people of Zamfara, to vote for APC from top to bottom in 2027. Vote for President Tinubu, vote for Governor Lawal, vote for our senators, House of Representatives members and State Assembly members. That is the only way Zamfara will move forward,” Yari said. He also urged voters to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, describing the President as the candidate capable of driving development in the North-West and the country. Yari said the Tinubu administration had demonstrated commitment to addressing insecurity, reviving the economy, improving infrastructure and repositioning the country for sustainable growth. He noted that the North-West, which had experienced years of banditry, kidnapping and economic challenges, needed sustained investment in security and development. “President Tinubu is the only candidate who, if given a second mandate, will develop the North-West and the country at large. He has the vision, the experience and the political will to take Nigeria to the next level. We must give him our full support,” he said. Yari called on Zamfara residents to give Tinubu substantial electoral support in 2027, as they did in 2023, to enable him to complete his reform agenda. He also canvassed support for Governor Lawal’s second-term ambition, saying the governor needed the backing of residents to consolidate his administration’s Rescue Zamfara Agenda. According to him, cooperation between the Federal Government and the Zamfara State Government would accelerate development in security, job creation, education, healthcare and infrastructure. The campaign launch was attended by APC stakeholders, government officials, members of the state executive council, federal and state lawmakers, local government chairmen, women and youth groups, and party supporters. item.title: 2027: No alliance between Otti, Orji Kalu — LP
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat. The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area. Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed. The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations. The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North. Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party. “The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none. “We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.” He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled. The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements. Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex. He said the party would not allow what it described as misleading political narratives to confuse its supporters across Arochukwu, Bende, Isuikwuato, Ohafia and Umunneochi local government areas. item.title: PSC appoints CP Usman Adamu Zamfara Police Commissioner
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the posting of CP Usman Sheikh Adamu as the new Commissioner of Police for Zamfara State. The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections. According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety. Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police. The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani. item.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
item.description: The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday. CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028. The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final. The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year. “The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.” The host cities and other details will be announced later. “We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani. “We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.” The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: CAF vows to enforce CAS ruling restoring Senegal’s AFCON title
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has pledged to implement the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruling that restored Senegal’s 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title following its dispute with Morocco. CAF made its position known in a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, saying it respected the decision of the Lausanne based tribunal and would take the necessary steps to give effect to it. “CAF respects the CAS Award and will take all the necessary measures to implement it,” the football governing body said. The CAS ruling overturned the CAF Appeal Board’s decision of March 17, 2026, which stripped Senegal of the title and awarded Morocco a 3-0 victory after ruling that the Teranga Lions had forfeited the final. Instead, the tribunal reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board, which had upheld Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the final played in Rabat on January 18, 2026. The dispute followed a controversial incident late in regulation time when Senegal’s players temporarily left the pitch after the referee awarded Morocco a penalty. The Senegalese players returned after about 14 minutes, but Morocco captain Brahim Diaz failed to convert the spot kick. Senegal later secured victory through Pape Gueye’s goal in extra time. Morocco subsequently challenged the result, arguing that Senegal had breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which address situations where a team abandons or refuses to continue a match. However, CAS ruled that the provisions did not apply because the referee had not permanently abandoned the match. The tribunal also held that the referee acted within his authority when he allowed play to resume. The decision was unanimous, according to CAS Secretary General Matthieu Reeb, who said the panel found no legal error in the referee’s handling of the incident. The tribunal’s ruling does not affect separate disciplinary sanctions imposed by CAF on Senegal coach Pape Thiaw and players Iliman Ndiaye and Ismaila Sarr over incidents during the final. Although CAF has promised to comply with the decision, it has not yet provided details of the administrative steps or a timeline for implementing the ruling. CAS confirmed that the full grounds for its decision had been communicated to the parties on Tuesday. The award is expected to be made public in due course, unless the parties request that it remain confidential. The ruling brings an end to the dispute over the final and restores Senegal’s second AFCON title, following its first triumph in 2021. item.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. item.title: Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has arrested a 30-year-old man, Tapro Tareza, for allegedly exhuming a corpse at Machika Cemetery in the Danko/Wasagu Local Government Area of the state. The suspect, a resident of Changu Village, Gwazawa, under Kanya District, was arrested following reports of repeated grave desecration at the cemetery. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday, saying the arrest followed a surveillance operation mounted by the police in collaboration with concerned youths in the community. According to him, on November 10, 2026, at about 7:15 p.m., shortly after the burial of a deceased person, the suspect was allegedly caught digging into the newly covered grave. Usman said vigilant youths apprehended him while he was allegedly committing the act and immediately alerted the police. He added that preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect allegedly removed items from the bodies of deceased persons. The police spokesman further said the suspect reportedly admitted involvement in previous acts of grave desecration at the same cemetery, including an earlier incident in which he allegedly removed and took away the burial shroud of a deceased person. Usman said investigations were ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incidents and ensure that the suspect faced appropriate legal action. The command commended members of the community for their vigilance and cooperation, while cautioning residents against taking the law into their own hands. It urged members of the public to promptly report suspicious activities to the police. The post Police arrest 30-year-old man for exhuming corpse in Kebbi appeared first on Vanguard News .

And I think it’s a moment that we should use to also assuage the challenges. “I’m aware that the federal government is providing CNG buses, you know, that are more economical. He said footage from the accident showed people boarding boats without life jackets, describing the practice as unacceptable and calling for tougher penalties against those who violated safety regulations. The basic idea is usually the same: match the numbers as they’re called and hope to complete your card before everyone else. But the rules, formats and even the way people play can vary quite a bit depending on where you are. Online bingo has made things even more interesting. Players aren’t restricted to their local halls anymore, and there are plenty of different versions to try without leaving the house. That means bigger prizes, more games to discover and plenty of social interaction with players from all over the world. And there’s certainly no shortage of choice. In the UK, 90-ball bingo is the traditional favourite. Cards have three rows and nine columns, with players looking to complete one line, two lines or a full house. It’s the format most people associate with a classic bingo night. Across the Atlantic, things are a little different. American bingo usually uses 75 balls and a five-by-five card, with players trying to complete particular patterns. These can include straight lines, diagonals, corners or more complicated shapes. Then there’s 80-ball bingo, which has become popular online. It uses a four-by-four card and offers a middle ground between the British and American formats. item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership. item.title: ‘This Is Payback Time’, Shettima Makes Case For Tinubu Re-Election In Borno
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima has urged voters in the North to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, describing it as an opportunity to reciprocate the president’s past political support for the region. Shettima made the appeal while speaking at the distribution and flag-off of special intervention projects by the North-East Development Commission (NEDC) in Borno State. He recalled that Tinubu played a significant role in securing the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket for former President Muhammadu Buhari ahead of the 2015 general election. According to the vice president, Tinubu deliberately moved the party’s presidential primary to Lagos and mobilised support for Buhari in the South-West, contributing to his emergence as the party’s candidate. “Those of us that were active in the political scene can bear testimony to the fact that without the efforts of President Bola Tinubu, Muhammadu Buhari couldn’t have clinched the ticket of the APC in 2014 in Lagos. “He deliberately shifted the base of the primaries to Lagos, and he worked assiduously to deliver the South-West. And one good turn always deserves another,” Shettima said. ﻿ The vice president urged the people of the North to reciprocate Tinubu’s political support by backing his re-election, declaring that the region had an opportunity to return the favour. “And for us in the North, this is payback time. I urge you, I beseech all of us here, let us use our informed judgment and make decisions that are in the best interest of our nation,” he said. Making a case for the administration’s economic policies, Shettima urged Nigerians to consider the government’s economic performance when deciding who to support in the 2027 elections. He cited a decline in headline inflation and an increase in the country’s foreign reserves, which he said had reached their highest level in 17 years. “The economy has turned the corner. Headline inflation has come down. Our foreign reserve is the highest in the past 17 years. It’s now hovering in the region of 55 billion dollars,” he said. Defending the removal of the petrol subsidy, the vice president maintained that the decision was not intended to worsen the economic hardship faced by Nigerians but to prevent the country’s economy from collapsing. “And the President has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy not to inflict pain on Nigerians, no. He removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said.
